message.text: An attacker posts email=admin@juice-sh.op'-- to POST /rest/user/login; the email is interpolated into the raw SQL string, the comment removes the password predicate, and the server issues a session token for the matched account; UNION payloads can also return arbitrary Users rows.

description.text: Parameterize the login query

trustBoundaries.rationale: Injected email bypasses the credential match, so a token is issued without a successful Users table credential check.
The login query bypasses Sequelize parameter binding and sends attacker text as raw SQL to SQLite.

message.text: An authenticated customer sets their username to #{global.process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('id')} via POST /profile (routes/updateUserProfile.ts:38), then opens GET /profile; routes/userProfile.ts:56 strips the #{ } wrapper and :61 passes the remainder to eval(), executing attacker JavaScript in the Node.js server process.

description.text: Remove server-side evaluation of untrusted input

message.text: A signed-in attacker puts another user's ID into the owner field of the request (req.body.UserId and the like); the query trusts it instead of the session identity, so the attacker reads or changes every other user's records — horizontal privilege escalation across all accounts.

description.text: Replace client-supplied owner ID with session-derived identity in every WHERE clause

message.text: An anonymous attacker requests GET /rest/products/search?q=')) UNION SELECT id,email,password,role,'5','6','7','8','9' FROM Users--; routes/search.ts:23 interpolates q into a raw sequelize.query and returns the result rows as products, disclosing every user's email and password hash.

description.text: Use parameterized database queries (F-005)

trustBoundaries.rationale: Search text reaches SQLite as raw SQL instead of a Sequelize bound parameter.

message.text: An attacker who knows the email of a user who signed in via Google OAuth computes btoa(reverse(email)) and submits it on the normal login form, because the OAuth component registered that account with exactly this derived password and logs in with it.

description.text: Replace derived OAuth password in oauth.component.ts with server-side identity linking

message.text: An attacker copies the RS256 private key literal from lib/insecurity.ts:21, signs a JWT whose data claim names any user or role=admin, and presents it as a Bearer token; isAuthorized() and verify() accept it because the matching public key validates the signature.

description.text: Move cryptographic keys to a managed secret store

trustBoundaries.rationale: isAuthorized() at the internet boundary trusts signatures made with a key published in source, so the authentication leg fails.

message.text: Decode-only flows let an attacker construct a token with any claims (admin, sub=victim, scope=*) — no key material required.

description.text: Manual review: verify JWT decode used without signature verification
Enforce JWT signature and algorithm verification (F-008)

message.text: An attacker sends a JWT with header alg:none (or HS256 keyed with the published public key) and an arbitrary data claim; isAuthorized() passes only the public key to express-jwt 0.1.3, verify() calls jws.verify(token, publicKey) without an algorithm, and updateAuthenticatedUsers() calls jwt.verify without algorithms, so the forged identity is accepted and cached in authenticatedUsers.

description.text: Manual review: verify Insecure JWT Verification at insecurity.ts:52
Pin RS256 algorithm allowlist in JWT verification

message.text: An attacker submits a victim email, a researched or guessed security answer, and a new password to POST /rest/user/reset-password; the handler compares only hmac(answer) with the stored answer and then sets the new password, taking over the account without any proof of mailbox or session ownership.

description.text: Replace security-question reset with emailed single-use token

trustBoundaries.rationale: Reset grants password change to anyone who knows the security answer, so reset is not restricted to the account owner.

message.text: A supply-chain attacker who takes over any direct or transitive npm package publishes a malicious version inside an accepted semver range; because .npmrc sets package-lock=false, the next Dockerfile `npm install --omit=dev` and the release `npm install --production` resolve it fresh and bake it into the published bkimminich/juice-shop image and release archives.

description.text: Commit lockfiles and install from them

message.text: A request-controlled path with `../` can read arbitrary files (/etc/passwd, source, secrets) or write outside the intended root.

description.text: Resolve the path and assert it stays within an allowed base directory

message.text: An anonymous attacker uploads a .zip to POST /file-upload whose entry is named ../../ftp/legal.md; extractZipBuffer at routes/fileUpload.ts:31 resolves 'uploads/complaints/' + entry.path and :33 only checks that the result contains the application root, so :34 overwrites any file inside the application directory.

description.text: Constrain file paths to a safe base directory

trustBoundaries.rationale: Uploaded archive entry names cross the internet boundary and reach a filesystem write without path validation.

message.text: Request input read at routes/trackOrder.ts:15 reaches an executable expression at routes/trackOrder.ts:18. Observed path conditions: const id = !utils.isChallengeEnabled(challenges.reflectedXssChallenge) ? String(req.params.id).replace(/[^\w-]+/g, '') : utils.trunc(req.params.id, 60). The unsafe path is observed; attacker control, access prerequisites, and active configuration require verification.

description.text: Use typed equality predicate instead of $where in routes/trackOrder.ts

trustBoundaries.rationale: The request path parameter is injected as executable JavaScript into a MarsDB $where operator.

message.text: Persisted record read at routes/userProfile.ts:41 reaches an executable expression at routes/userProfile.ts:87. Observed path conditions: if (username) {. The unsafe path is observed; attacker control, access prerequisites, and active configuration require verification.

description.text: Keep input as data; remove dynamic code or template-source compilation
Manual review: verify Input compiled as template source at userProfile.ts:87

message.text: An attacker who achieves any script execution in the shop origin (for example the search DOM XSS) reads localStorage.token and the JS-set token cookie and replays the bearer token against the API from their own machine.

description.text: Move session token from localStorage to HttpOnly cookie

message.text: An attacker who completes a security-question reset receives res.json({ user: updatedUser }) containing the entire Users row, including totpSecret, and uses that seed to generate TOTP codes and pass 2FA on the hijacked account.

description.text: Stop exposing internal information to clients

message.text: An attacker who obtains any session token (browser storage, logs, or XSS) base64-decodes its payload and reads the user's MD5 password hash and, for 2FA users, the plaintext totpSecret, then cracks the hash and generates valid TOTP codes to log in with both factors.

description.text: Manual review: verify Password hash and TOTP secret in JWT payload at 2fa.ts:42
Minimize JWT claims in routes/2fa.ts and routes/login.ts

message.text: An attacker who extracts Users.password values (via the login SQL injection or a JWT payload) recovers plaintext passwords with rainbow tables or GPU cracking because hash() is a single unsalted MD5.

description.text: Hash passwords with a strong, salted algorithm

message.text: An anonymous attacker requests GET /rest/memories; routes/memory.ts:24 runs MemoryModel.findAll({ include: [UserModel] }) without an attributes filter, so every memory carries its author's full User row including email, MD5 password hash, role, and totpSecret.

description.text: Restrict included user attributes

message.text: An anonymous attacker uploads complaint.xml declaring <!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd"> to POST /file-upload; lib/xml.ts:22 registers host filesystem input providers and :35 parses with XML_PARSE_NOENT|XML_PARSE_DTDLOAD, and routes/fileUpload.ts:79 echoes up to 400 characters of the expanded document in the error response.

description.text: Disable XML external entity (XXE) resolution

message.text: An authenticated customer posts imageUrl=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/x.png to /profile/image/url; routes/profileImageUrlUpload.ts:24 fetches it server-side with no scheme or host allow-list and :29-30 writes the body to a publicly served uploads file, which the attacker then downloads.

description.text: Validate and allowlist outbound request targets

message.text: An attacker reads the public repository or shipped server bundle, derives the private key from the embedded BIP-39 mnemonic with HDNodeWallet.fromPhrase, and submits it to POST /rest/web3/submitKey to unlock the NFT challenge, while also gaining signing control of that Ethereum wallet.

description.text: Move secrets to a managed secret store (F-024)

message.text: An anonymous attacker connects to the Socket.IO endpoint and emits verifySvgInjectionChallenge with a non-string payload such as 1 or {}; data?.match resolves to undefined and the call throws a TypeError inside the event listener, which Socket.IO dispatches outside any try/catch, so unless a process-level handler exists the Node process terminates for all users.

description.text: Validate socket payload types

message.text: LLM06/ASI02: an anonymous attacker uses injected chat turns (express-api-008) to make the model call generateCoupon with discount 99; routes/chat.ts:179 declares discount as an unconstrained z.number() and :184 mints the coupon with no server-side check of caller, order, eligibility, or the 10% ceiling stated only in the prompt, and the coupon is redeemable for up to 99% off.

description.text: Enforce server-side authorization on every endpoint (F-026)

trustBoundaries.rationale: LLM output selects and parameterizes a consequential tool without server-side validation of the model's decision.

message.text: The route registration carries no authentication marker, so an anonymous attacker may call this state-changing operation on a sensitive resource directly, unless a downstream check the scanner cannot see stops it.

description.text: Add explicit authentication middleware to the /profile/image/file route
Manual review: verify Sensitive Routes Registered Without Authentication Middleware

message.text: An anonymous attacker sends PUT /api/Products/1 with a new price or description; server.ts guards POST and DELETE on /api/Products but no middleware covers PUT, so the finale resource generated at server.ts:501 applies the update.

description.text: Manual review: verify Unauthenticated product update via finale at server.ts:501
Deny product updates

trustBoundaries.rationale: A state-changing generated route is not registered behind isAuthorized(), breaking the authentication leg.

message.text: An anonymous attacker posts {"email":"x@y.z","password":"p","passwordRepeat":"p","role":"accounting"} to POST /api/Users; the finale resource at server.ts:501 creates the user from the whole body and the role setter at models/user.ts:97 stores any value in the isIn list, so the attacker's next login token carries the accounting or admin role.

description.text: Manual review: verify Mass-assigned role on user registration at user.ts:97
Allowlist client-controlled fields

message.text: An attacker sends a victim a link to /#access_token=<attacker Google token>; the OAuth component accepts any fragment token because the flow uses response_type=token without a state value, logging the victim into the attacker's account (login CSRF).

description.text: Add anti-CSRF protection to state-changing requests

message.text: An attacker who obtains a victim's JWT keeps using it for up to six hours after the victim resets the password or disables and re-enables 2FA, because tokens are stateless, authenticatedUsers.tokenMap entries are never deleted, and no handler invalidates prior tokens.

description.text: Add server-side token revocation to authenticatedUsers

message.text: An attacker reads a minter address from public NFTMinted events on Sepolia and posts it as walletAddress to walletNFTVerify; the handler only checks set membership, so it marks the NFT mint challenge solved and consumes that address without any signature proving the caller controls the wallet.

description.text: Require signed wallet challenge

message.text: An anonymous attacker sends victims a shop link /redirect?to=<url> whose target passes security.isRedirectAllowed without starting with an allowlisted URL; performRedirect then issues res.redirect(toUrl) to the attacker-controlled site, lending the shop's origin to a phishing page.

description.text: Validate redirect targets against an allowlist

message.text: An attacker who gets markup into data included in a user's export (for example stored profile or review text) has it executed when the user exports data, because the response is written with document.write into a same-origin about:blank window.

description.text: Deliver data export as a JSON download

message.text: Missing Container Image Signing: Unsigned container images cannot be verified for provenance — any registry intermediary could substitute them.

description.text: Add cosign signing or SLSA provenance attestation to release workflow

message.text: An attacker who controls or intercepts cli-assets.heroku.com serves a modified install.sh; the heroku job pipes it straight into sh and the next step hands HEROKU_API_KEY to the tampered CLI, which exfiltrates the key or deploys attacker code to the juice-shop Heroku apps.

description.text: Install Heroku CLI from a pinned, checksum-verified artifact

message.text: Dependency Install Scripts Run at Build Time: Without --ignore-scripts, any compromised dependency publisher can execute postinstall code at build time.

description.text: Use `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in Dockerfile and workflows; audit necessary postinstalls

message.text: An attacker who compromises the calibreapp/image-actions repository pushes malicious code to its main branch; the next image push to master or develop executes it with the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN passed as githubToken, letting it rewrite repository images or commit content.

description.text: Pin third-party dependencies to immutable versions (F-038)

message.text: An attacker who compromises the node:24 or gcr.io/distroless/nodejs24-debian13 tag, or the registry path, substitutes a backdoored image; the next CI or release build pulls it by tag and the published Juice Shop image inherits the backdoor.

description.text: Pin Dockerfile base images to sha256 digests

message.text: An authenticated customer sends PATCH /rest/products/reviews with {"id":{"$ne":-1},"message":"x"}; routes/updateProductReviews.ts:18 uses req.body.id directly as the MarsDB selector with multi:true at :20, overwriting every product review, and no check compares the review author with the caller.

description.text: Constrain review update selector and owner in routes/updateProductReviews.ts

trustBoundaries.rationale: Untrusted request objects reach the MarsDB selector as query operators.

message.text: LLM01/ASI01: an anonymous attacker posts to /rest/chat a messages array containing fabricated system, assistant, or tool turns (for example a fake 'verified damaged order' tool result); routes/chat.ts:191 takes req.body.messages verbatim and :206 forwards it to streamText, so the attacker rewrites the conversation the model reasons over and overrides the policy written in the system prompt.

description.text: Accept only user-role text and server-held history in routes/chat.ts

trustBoundaries.rationale: Attacker-controlled conversation turns reach the LLM prompt unfiltered, breaking the egress-content assumption.

message.text: An anonymous attacker opens a Socket.IO connection without any token and emits verifyCloseNotificationsChallenge with [1,2] (or crafted verifyLocalXssChallenge/verifySvgInjectionChallenge payloads), which the server accepts and marks the challenges solved for the whole instance; the same unauthenticated socket can emit 'notification received' with a broadcast flag to delete that notification from the shared list for every client.

description.text: Require authentication on every exposed endpoint

message.text: An attacker brute-forces logins, abuses the security-question reset, or disables a victim's 2FA; failed logins at routes/login.ts:50, password resets at routes/resetPassword.ts:44, and 2FA changes in routes/2fa.ts emit no security log entry, so the account owner and operators cannot reconstruct or attribute the takeover.

description.text: Add security audit logging

message.text: An anonymous attacker sends PUT /rest/products/1/reviews with author set to another customer's email; routes/createProductReviews.ts:26 stores req.body.author as the review author even though the authenticated user, when present, is read at :16 and ignored, so the review is attributed to the victim.

description.text: Derive review author from verified session in routes/createProductReviews.ts

message.text: An attacker manipulates the chatbot into calling generateCoupon; routes/chat.ts:184 mints the coupon and returns it while the only record is a Prometheus counter increment at :227, so operators cannot reconstruct which caller, prompt, model response, or discount produced a coupon later redeemed.

description.text: Audit-log coupon tool calls in routes/chat.ts

message.text: An attacker downloads the public JavaScript bundle, extracts testing@juice-sh.op / IamU**** (17 chars) from the LoginComponent class, and tries them on the login form.

description.text: Move secrets to a managed secret store (F-046)

message.text: An authenticated customer posts to /dataerasure with layout=../package.json; routes/dataErasure.ts:104-105 rejects only paths containing ftp, ctf.key, or encryptionkeys, and :107 spreads req.body into res.render options so the view engine loads the attacker-named file as the layout and returns its first 100 characters.

description.text: Stop passing request body to res.render in routes/dataErasure.ts

message.text: An anonymous attacker browses /support/logs; server.ts:281 serves a directory index of logs/ and :283 serves each file, exposing morgan combined access logs with client IPs, request URLs, and user agents of all visitors.

description.text: Remove public log directory routes from server.ts

message.text: An anonymous attacker connects a Socket.IO client to a shared CTF-mode instance and receives every 'challenge solved' notification, each carrying the ctfFlag value, both live via io.emit and replayed on connect, then submits other players' flags to the CTF scoring server without solving the challenges.

description.text: Scope challenge notifications to authenticated sockets

message.text: An attacker holding a tmpToken from a correct password replays POST /rest/2fa/verify with successive 6-digit codes, and separately sprays passwords at POST /rest/user/login; neither handler counts failures or locks the account, so guessing proceeds at request rate.

description.text: Rate-limit and lock out repeated authentication attempts

message.text: An anonymous attacker repeatedly uploads a 200 kB YAML alias bomb or XML billion-laughs file to POST /file-upload; routes/fileUpload.ts:109 runs yaml.load inside vm.runInContext with a 2000 ms timeout (and lib/xml.ts:38 likewise for XML), which executes synchronously on the event loop, so each upload freezes the whole server for up to two seconds.

description.text: Move untrusted parsing off event loop in routes/fileUpload.ts

message.text: LLM10/ASI08: an anonymous attacker scripts parallel POST /rest/chat requests with long messages arrays; server.ts:638 applies no authentication or rate limit and routes/chat.ts:203 calls streamText with no maxOutputTokens or input size bound, allowing up to 10 tool steps per request, so the attacker exhausts the Ollama backend and its token budget.

description.text: Rate-limit and token-cap /rest/chat in routes/chat.ts

message.text: An anonymous attacker requests GET /rest/products/sleep(2000)/reviews repeatedly; routes/showProductReviews.ts:31 keeps up to 40 characters of the id when the noSqlCommand challenge is enabled and :36 concatenates it into a MarsDB $where predicate evaluated in-process, so each request runs attacker JavaScript that blocks the single Node.js event loop.

description.text: Replace $where with numeric equality in routes/showProductReviews.ts

trustBoundaries.rationale: The URL id is injected as executable JavaScript into a MarsDB $where operator.

message.text: An attacker fires a burst of concurrent requests to the NFT listener endpoint; because isEventListenerCreated is only set at line 29 after the awaited import, and the onerror handler resets it without destroying the old provider, each request opens a new WebSocketProvider to Alchemy with the shared ALCHEMY_API_KEY.

description.text: Create single listener via shared promise

trustBoundaries.rationale: Every leaked provider crosses the operator boundary to Alchemy using the shared ALCHEMY_API_KEY, so the egress is unbounded.

message.text: An attacker places a hand-crafted unsigned JWT with data.role=admin in localStorage; AdminGuard decodes it without signature verification and opens /administration, leaving all protection of admin data to whatever the API enforces.

description.text: Enforce authorization on the server

message.text: A compromised step such as calibreapp/image-actions@main receives GITHUB_TOKEN at image_actions.yml:35; because the workflow declares no permissions block, the token inherits the repository default scope, which, if set to read-write, lets the attacker push commits, create releases or alter workflows.

description.text: Drop unnecessary privileges in build and runtime

message.text: Container Runs as Root: Containers running as root expand container-escape blast radius.

description.text: Add non-root USER directive to test/smoke/Dockerfile

message.text: Missing Workflow Permissions Block: Without an explicit permissions block at workflow or job level, the job inherits the repository default (commonly write-all) for GITHUB_TOKEN — any compromised step can push code, create releases, or approve PRs.

description.text: Add top-level read-only permissions block to all workflows lacking one

message.text: Token exfiltrated from local/session storage via the Step 1 payload.

description.text: Store session tokens in HttpOnly cookies

message.text: Exfiltrated token accepted for a new session; absence of token binding / PKCE removes the last server-side revocation opportunity.
